title: Transient middle cerebral artery occlusion with complete reperfusion in spontaneously hypertensive rats
author: Hill, Nemoto

steps.title: Anesthetize and position animal
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with 2 % isoflurane inhalant and place the rat supine on a surgical table with a 15 ml tube under the neck to improve visualization of neck vessels.

steps.title: Prepare neck incision
steps.instruction: Shave the neck, disinfect with povidone‑iodine solution, then clean with 70 % ethyl alcohol.

steps.title: Expose right common carotid artery
steps.instruction: Make a shallow 25 mm midline incision from the base of the mandible to the sternum, retract the sternohyoid and sternomastoid muscles, and separate the right CCA from the vagus nerve.

steps.title: Ligate and clamp CCA
steps.instruction: Tie a 4‑0 silk suture with a single knot 6–7 mm caudal to the CCA bifurcation (ECA/ICA), place a vascular clamp immediately caudal to the bifurcation, and loosely tie two additional 4‑0 silk sutures around the CCA between the first suture and the clamp.

steps.title: Create ventral CCA incision
steps.instruction: Using a 25 G needle, make a punctate incision in the ventral wall of the CCA 5 mm caudal to the clamp.

steps.title: Insert occluding suture
steps.instruction: Advance a 4‑0 nylon suture (Doccol Corp.) 30 mm long with a 2–3 mm silicone‑coated tip (0.39 mm diameter) into the CCA lumen up to the clamp; secure the lower silk suture around the occluding suture to prevent bleeding.

steps.title: Advance suture into ICA
steps.instruction: Remove the clamp and push the suture into the ICA until resistance is felt; if resistance occurs while most of the suture remains outside the field, withdraw to the bifurcation and re‑insert directing toward the midline.

steps.title: Confirm proper placement
steps.instruction: Grasp the suture with forceps, bend it toward the midline, and gently push forward until flexion of the suture is visualized through the lateral ICA wall; do not advance past this point to avoid ICA puncture or subarachnoid hemorrhage, and visualize flexion only once.

steps.title: Secure occluding suture
steps.instruction: Tighten the two loose silk sutures around the CCA and trim the excess occluding suture with micro scissors; the suture now occludes the MCA origin.

steps.title: Close wound and start occlusion
steps.instruction: Close the surgical wound and allow the animal to recover for a 90‑min MCA occlusion period.

steps.title: Re‑anesthetize and expose field
steps.instruction: After 90 min, re‑induce anesthesia with 2 % isoflurane and re‑expose the surgical field.

steps.title: Withdraw occluding suture
steps.instruction: Loosen the upper silk suture, pull the occluding suture back to the middle suture, move the upper suture rostrally and secure it around the CCA above the silicone tip, then remove the middle and occluding sutures.

steps.title: Clamp CCA rostrally
steps.instruction: Place a vascular clamp 1 mm rostral to the CCA incision; the incision is now visible on the vessel surface and the lumen is closed.

steps.title: Apply first adhesive drop
steps.instruction: Place the bevel‑up tip of a clean 25 G needle into a ~0.25 mm thick drop of tissue adhesive (verified under a microscope) and apply the adhesive directly onto the incision; remove the clamp after 1 min.

steps.title: Create adhesive patch
steps.instruction: Using a second clean 25 G needle, apply another drop of adhesive around the first to form a circular patch ≈0.5 mm in diameter; allow the adhesive to cure for 2 min.

steps.title: Check for leakage and finalize closure
steps.instruction: Loosen the rostral silk suture and inspect the patch; if leakage is observed, re‑secure the suture and add a minimal amount of adhesive to expand the patch. Once secure, carefully remove the lower silk suture, verify perfusion through the CCA, close the wound, and inject 3 ml subcutaneous normal saline to prevent dehydration.

description: All animal procedures were approved by the University of New Mexico Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee and were in compliance with federal guidelines. Animals were anesthetized with 2% isoflurane inhalant during all surgical procedures.
